questions.q: What is the point-in-time rule for a label at time T?
options: Use the latest feature value with feature time at or before T
Use the average of all feature values
Use the feature value nearest to T in either direction
Use the final value after all corrections
why: Correct. This is what the model could know at T.
Averaging all values includes the future.
Nearest can be later than T. That is leakage.
Final values contain later corrections that did not exist at T.

questions.q: Which merge_asof argument rejects feature values that are too old?
options: by
tolerance
allow_exact_matches
direction
why: `by` matches inside each entity.
Correct: tolerance sets the maximum age of the match.
This only decides whether an equal timestamp may match.
Direction chooses backward, forward or nearest.

questions.q: Which are signs of training-serving skew? (pick all)
options: Feature is written in SQL for training and in Java for serving
Feature mean in serving logs differs from the training set
Model is retrained every week
A feature is null online but never null offline
why: Two code paths drift apart over time.
A shifted distribution points to a different computation.
A weekly schedule is normal and not a skew.
Nulls only online mean the online pipeline is late or broken.

questions.q: Scenario: your daily feature 'avg_price' is computed at 23:00 and stored with date = that day. You join labels at 10:00 on the same date by date. What happens?
options: Nothing, the date is the same
Leakage: the 10:00 label sees a value computed at 23:00
The join drops the row
The value is stale by one day
why: The dates match, but the value did not exist at 10:00.
Correct. Use the timestamp when the value became available.
A date join keeps the row.
It is the opposite: it is too new, not too old.

questions.q: Scenario: labels at 12:00 and 18:00. Feature rows at 06:00 (value 5) and 20:00 (value 9). With tolerance=8h, what values do the labels get (12:00, 18:00)?
options: 5 and 9
5 and 5
5 and NaN
NaN and NaN
why: 9 is at 20:00, after 18:00. It is the future.
18:00 is 12 hours after 06:00. That is more than 8 hours.
Correct: 12:00 is 6 hours after 06:00 (inside tolerance). 18:00 is 12 hours after (too old), so NaN.
12:00 is only 6 hours after 06:00, so it gets 5.

questions.q: A feature is recomputed daily at 02:00 and has values 100 (Mon), 120 (Tue), 90 (Wed). A label arrives on Wed 01:00. Which value is point-in-time correct?
questions.why: Wed 02:00 is after 01:00, so it is not known yet. The latest known value is Tue 02:00 = 120.
